introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 2 (0550), Paper 2, ORDINARY LEVEL, JUNE 2024. Duration: Two and a Half Hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR Questions choosing ONE from each section.

Question ONE carries 30 marks. All the other Questions carry 20 marks each.

Each question that is sub-divided has the sub marks in brackets.

In questions involving calculations, all steps of the working MUST be shown.

If an outline MAP and/or GRAPH are used, they must be tied inside your answer booklet, opposite the written part of the answer.

NB - ONLY THE FIRST FOUR QUESTIONS ANSWERED WILL BE MARKED.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) On the outline map of Cameroon provided, locate and name the following

![fig-1](gce-ol-geography-2024-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_6_fig_1.png)

(i) One drainage basin
(ii) A National Park
(iii) An area covered by mangrove forest
(iv) The political and economic capitals of Cameroon
(v) Belabo-Ngouandere Railway line

(7 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The outline map (printed on a separate page of the paper, shown above) has the **north arrow** at the top and the **Gulf of Guinea coast in the south-west**, the **Lake Chad** area in the extreme north and the long narrow **Far North** in the north-east. Each feature is located by a **mark** (a point, a line or a shaded area), a **name** written next to it and, if there is room, a **key**. The positions below are described in words relative to the outline (at the scale of the outline map, an error of a few millimetres is accepted).

| Item | What to draw and name | Where on the outline map |
|---|---|---|
| (i) **One drainage basin** | The **Lake Chad basin** (Logone and Chari rivers) | extreme north and Far North region, around Lake Chad at the top of the map; shade the area and write "Lake Chad basin" |
| | *or* the **Benue (Niger) basin** | the north and north-west, drained to the River Benue; *or* the **Atlantic basin** (Sanaga, Wouri, Nyong, Cross River) in the south-west and centre; *or* the **Congo basin** (Sangha) in the south-east |
| (ii) **A National Park** | **Waza National Park** | in the Far North, south of Lake Chad and east of the Mandara Mountains |
| | *or* **Korup National Park** | in the South-West region, near the border with Nigeria; *or* **Benoue National Park** in the North |
| (iii) **An area covered by mangrove forest** | **The coast of the Gulf of Guinea round the Wouri estuary** (Douala), the Rio del Rey estuary, the mouth of the Cross River and the area round the Cameroon estuary | along the **south-west coast**, shaded as a strip along the Atlantic Ocean at the Bight of Biafra |
| (iv) **The political and economic capitals** | **Yaounde** (political capital) | in the interior of the south, in the Centre region, a little inland from the coast |
| | **Douala** (economic capital, the main seaport) | on the **Atlantic coast**, at the head of the Wouri estuary, south-west of Yaounde |
| (v) **Belabo-Ngaoundere railway line** | The **railway** from Yaounde to Belabo (East) and from Belabo **north** to **Ngaoundere** (Adamawa plateau), which is the terminus of the line | draw a line from Belabo (east-centre) north-north-east to Ngaoundere (north-centre, at the Adamawa plateau), marking both towns |

**Marking guide (7 marks):** (i) 1, (ii) 1, (iii) 1.5, (iv) 2 (1 each), (v) 1.5; one mark for the **correct position** and a half mark for the **name** for each (if both are required).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) (i) Name TWO areas of high population density
(ii) For any one of them explain three reasons for the high population density

(2 + 6 = 8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Two areas of high population density in Cameroon (2 marks, 1 mark each).**

1. The **Western Highlands**: the **West region (Bamileke plateau)** and the **North-West region (Bamenda highlands)**.
2. The **coastal and urban areas** of the **Littoral (Douala)** and of the **Centre (Yaounde)**.

(Other correct areas: the Mandara Mountains in the Far North, the Mount Cameroon area, the Logone floodplain.)

**(ii) Three reasons for the high population density of the Western Highlands (6 marks, 2 marks each: the reason and its explanation).**

1. **Fertile volcanic soils.** The volcanic soils of the plateau and the slopes of the old volcanoes are rich and allow intensive farming (maize, beans, plantains, vegetables, coffee), so that the land can feed many people on a small area.
2. **A cool and healthy climate.** Because of the altitude (the plateau lies at more than about 1000 m), temperatures are lower than on the coast and in the lowlands, the climate is pleasant and there are fewer diseases such as malaria and no tsetse fly, so people settled and stayed there.
3. **Reliable rainfall and good water supply.** Rain is abundant for most of the year, with many streams, which favours agriculture and the settlement of people.
4. **Economic activities and services.** Strong **trade and small industries**, big markets and towns (Bafoussam, Bamenda), good roads linking the highlands to Douala and **traditional chiefdoms** with a strong social organisation that favoured the **growth of the population** over a long time also attract migrants.

(Any three reasons are required.)

*If the Douala (Littoral) area is chosen:* the reasons would be the **port and the main industries** (jobs), the **commercial and administrative functions**, **rural-urban migration** and the **services** (schools, hospitals, electricity) concentrated in the city.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) What efforts are being made by the government of Cameroon to emerge by 2035 in the domain of agriculture.

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Cameroon's long-term plan, **Vision 2035**, aims to make the country an **emerging**, democratic and united country, with agriculture as a key sector. It is put into effect through medium-term strategies (the Growth and Employment Strategy Paper for 2010 to 2019 and, after it, the National Development Strategy for 2020 to 2030). In the domain of agriculture, the government is making the following efforts (5 marks, 1 mark each; any five):

1. **Modernising agriculture** (the "second generation agriculture" policy): encouraging **mechanisation** and the use of **fertilizers, improved seeds and plant protection products**, and supporting medium-sized and large farms as well as family farms.
2. **Agricultural support programmes** and projects financed by the State and by development partners (for example programmes to improve the competitiveness of family farms and the marketing of farm produce), to raise output and incomes of farmers.
3. **Training and extension services:** the training of farmers and of technicians by the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development, and agricultural **research** (for example by the Institute of Agricultural Research for Development, IRAD) to produce improved varieties and methods.
4. **Rural infrastructure:** building **rural roads, stores, markets and processing units** to reduce post-harvest losses and to bring the produce to the markets.
5. **Financing and organising farmers:** access to **credit** (including microfinance), support for **cooperatives and farmers' groups**, and the development of **agro-industries** for the processing of cocoa, coffee, cotton, palm oil, rubber and sugar so that Cameroon exports **processed products** and not only raw materials.
6. Efforts to **increase the area under cultivation and the production of food and cash crops** to ensure **food security** and to reduce the importation of food (rice, wheat, fish), and to improve livestock and fishing activities.
